title: $Lf^*$, $Rf_*$, $j_!$, $\otimes^{\mathrm L}$, $\RHom$ on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$: restrictions
statement:
Fix distinct primes $p$ and $\ell$ and a field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. All schemes below are separated and of finite type over $k$, and all morphisms are morphisms of $k$-schemes, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring ([sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]). Consider the following functors on the ambient derived categories of module objects:

- the derived pullback $Lf^*\colon D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ and the derived
  pushforward $Rf_*\colon D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$ of a morphism
  $f\colon X\to Y$ ([sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]);
- the extension by zero $j_!=D(j_!)\colon D(\Mod_{\Lambda_U})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ along an
  open immersion $j\colon U\to X$, applied levelwise to complexes
  ([sk-def-sfb-module-lower-shriek], [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek]);
- the derived tensor product $-\otimes^{\mathrm L}_{\Lambda_X}-$ and the derived internal hom
  $\RHom_{\Lambda_X}(-,-)$ on $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_X})$ ([sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]).

Each of them carries bounded constructible complexes ([sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]) to
bounded constructible complexes in the following cases. For $Lf^*$ and $j_!$ this holds for every
$\Lambda$. For $Rf_*$, $\otimes^{\mathrm L}$ and $\RHom$ it holds for the $\ell$-adic rings
$\Lambda=\underline{\cO}_E$, $\underline E$ ($E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite;
[sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]) and $\Lambda=\underline{\Qlb}$ ([sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]); these
are Deligne's finiteness theorems. It fails for a general $\Lambda$.

When the preservation property holds, the functor on $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is defined as the
**restriction** of the ambient functor: it is the unique functor whose composite with the fully
faithful inclusion $D_{\mathrm{cons}}\subseteq D(\Mod)$ equals the composite of the inclusion with
the ambient functor. This gives

$$
\begin{gathered}
Lf^*\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda),\qquad
Rf_*\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(Y,\Lambda),\qquad
j_!\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(U,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda),\\
-\otimes^{\mathrm L}-\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)\times D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda),\qquad
\RHom(-,-)\colon D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)^{\mathrm{op}}\times D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)\to D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda).
\end{gathered}
$$

By construction they commute with the inclusions. Nothing is derived afresh. The following
structure is also restricted along the fully faithful inclusions:

- the adjunctions $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, $j_!\dashv Lj^*$, and $K\otimes^{\mathrm L}-\dashv\RHom(K,-)$ for
  $K\in D_{\mathrm{cons}}(X,\Lambda)$;
- the composition isomorphism $L(g\circ f)^*\cong Lf^*\circ Lg^*$ for $f\colon X\to Y$,
  $g\colon Y\to Z$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dc-upper-star-preserves] to $f$ and [lem-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-preserves] to $j$: these give preservation for every commutative condensed $\Lambda$. Apply [lem-sfb-dc-lower-star-preserves], [lem-sfb-dc-tensor-preserves] and [lem-sfb-dc-hom-preserves] with $\Lambda=\underline{\cO}_E,\underline E,\underline{\Qlb}$: these give exactly the three remaining preservation assertions. Each cited statement assumes the same setting as this item, and the latter three assume exactly the coefficient cases asserted here. In particular none of those three is being applied to an arbitrary condensed ring.

By [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], an object of $D_{\mathrm{cons}}$ is an ambient derived object equipped with its bounded-constructibility property, and its morphisms are the ambient morphisms. For any one of the operations $F$ covered by step 1, send $(K,h_K)$ to $(F(K),h_{F(K)})$, using the applicable preservation assertion from step 1, and send $a$ to $F(a)$. For tensor and internal Hom do this on the product and the opposite-product full subcategories respectively. Identity and composition laws are those of the ambient $F$. Forgetting the property recovers $F$ on objects and morphisms, so the inclusions commute with these functors. Conversely any restriction commuting with these inclusions has precisely these underlying objects and maps; the attached properties introduce no additional choices. This is the restriction construction of [def-sfb-dc-upper-star], [def-sfb-dc-lower-star], [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek], [def-sfb-dc-tensor] and [def-sfb-dc-hom], and gives all the displayed functors without deriving anything anew.

proof.text: The statements [def-sfb-dc-upper-lower-adjunction], [def-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-adjunction] and [def-sfb-dc-tensor-hom-adjunction] specify the three adjunctions as the ambient Hom-bijections on the indicated restricted objects. In particular, the second statement includes the ambient identification $D(j^*)\cong Lj^*$; no identification of unrelated coefficient categories is used. For each pair of bounded constructible objects, the full-subcategory Hom-sets are exactly the ambient Hom-sets, so these bijections and their inverses have the required source and target. Their naturality equations are the ambient equations on the same morphisms. They therefore give the asserted restricted adjunctions. For $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ use the coefficients for which $Rf_*$ preserves; for $j_!\dashv Lj^*$ use any $\Lambda$; for tensor–Hom require both preservation properties and fix $K$ bounded constructible, exactly as in the cited statements.

source.place: sk-def-sfb-dc-restricted-functors.proof.md, second paragraph: restriction of the adjunctions

proof.text: Use the composition isomorphism specified by [def-sfb-dc-upper-star-comp]. At each bounded constructible $K$ its component and inverse are the ambient composition-isomorphism component and its inverse, regarded as maps in the full subcategory. Their two composites are identities and their naturality squares commute because the corresponding ambient equations hold. Faithfulness of the inclusion proves uniqueness of this natural isomorphism with its prescribed ambient image. Its hypotheses allow every commutative condensed $\Lambda$ and composable morphisms of the setting, as required.
